keyword: are they landing on the moon

verifications.claim: As of April 1, 2026, the Artemis II crew is flying around the Moon.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "The crew will spend about 24 hours orbiting the Earth while they put their Orion capsule through its paces before finally heading for the moon." (R1); launch on April 1 evening, lunar flyby on April 6 (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Launch occurred on evening of April 1, 2026; crew spent first ~24 hours in Earth orbit testing systems, not yet flying around the Moon (lunar flyby ~April 6).

verifications.claim: As of April 1, 2026, the Artemis II crew is not landing on the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The Artemis crew will not land on the moon or even go into lunar orbit. Instead, the plan is to loop around it" (R1); "will take astronauts around the moon but not land there" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm Artemis II does not land on the Moon; it flies around it, and this was the plan from launch on April 1.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consists of four astronauts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen" (R1); consistently lists four astronauts across sources
verifications.reasoning: Every reference explicitly names or states the crew of four astronauts.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew launched on a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "~10-day mission" (cited snippet); "about nine and a half days" from April 1 to April 10 splashdown (R1); "10-day mission" (R2, R4, R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources uniformly describe the mission duration as approximately 10 days, with launch April 1 and splashdown April 10.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is to test systems for future landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Crew manually took control of the Orion capsule as part of a test to ensure certain capabilities for future missions, including the ability to dock with a lunar lander" (R1); "mimicked the maneuvers that will be used during later missions for docking with lunar landers" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Mission explicitly tests docking, navigation, and other systems needed for future lunar landing missions like Artemis III/IV.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew are the first humans to travel to the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago" (R1, 1972+53=2025 approx.); "first time humans have returned to the moon since the last Apollo mission in 1972" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All sources state Artemis II is the first crewed mission to the Moon vicinity since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: A human lunar landing is planned for a future mission targeted for 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "at least one lunar landing in 2028" (R1); "putting new footprints on the moon by the end of 2028" (R2); "Artemis IV mission... in 2028" (R4); "land people on the Moon in 2028" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm NASA plans a human lunar landing (Artemis III/IV) targeted for 2028.
